jurisdiction.name: Organization of American States
jurisdiction.overview: Official documents of this organisation are listed on its own page and are not counted in member countries' totals.

narrative.summary: The OAS's main AI-related texts so far come from its Inter-American Juridical Committee, which adopted a 2021 declaration and, in 2023, a set of ten Inter-American principles on neuroscience, neurotechnologies and human rights that address AI-linked neural data processing. The OAS Secretariat published draft Inter-American Guidelines on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence for regional public consultation in November 2024. Ministers of science and technology adopted a declaration and plan of action on safe, secure and trustworthy AI in the Americas in December 2024.
lead_institutions: OAS General Secretariat (Department for Effective Public Management)

instruments.summary: Draft guidelines forming part of the Inter-American Framework of Reference for Data Governance and AI (MIGDIA). They set out a roadmap across twelve thematic areas to help OAS Member States develop national data and AI governance frameworks and to serve as a reference for local governments.
instruments.current_status: Published by the OAS in English and Spanish for an open regional public consultation in November 2024. Final adoption has not been announced on the OAS site.
instruments.evidence_reference: OAS event page 'Open regional public consultation: inter-American guidelines on data governance and AI' lists start date 11/8/2024 (US format = 8 Nov 2024) and links the guidelines in EN/ES; month only given because the exact day format is ambiguous. Derechos Digitales commentary says the draft was published 12 Nov and presented at the Red GEALC ministerial 26-27 Nov 2024, with approval expected at the 2025 Summit of the Americas; no evidence of final adoption found. OECD.AI hosts a copy (Publicación_Lineamientos_19-11-24_ENG.pdf) — not an official OAS URL, so not used.

leads.title: AG/RES. 3013 (LIV-O/24) Impulsando iniciativas hemisféricas en materia de desarrollo integral: promoción de la resiliencia
leads.note: Omnibus OAS General Assembly resolution (Asunción, June 2024) with two operative paragraphs (8-9) on AI cooperation and centres of excellence; no dedicated AI section. Text seen only on a non-OAS mirror of AG/doc.5871/24.

leads.title: Inter-American Juridical Committee agenda item: Impact of AI-based technologies on human rights, with a special focus on children and adolescents
leads.note: Ongoing study topic (rapporteurs Orias Arredondo and Valencia Gartner) on the IAJC agenda since 2024; no adopted principles or guide found yet.

leads.title: Joint Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Freedom of Expression (UN, OSCE, OAS/IACHR Special Rapporteur, ACHPR freedom of expression mandates)
leads.note: Issued by independent special rapporteurs including the IACHR Special Rapporteur for Freedom of Expression; not a formally adopted text of the IACHR or OAS member states.

leads.title: Declaración Ministerial de Santo Domingo — IX Ministerial Meeting on Digital Government of the Americas / Red GEALC (29 Sep - 2 Oct 2026)
leads.note: Reported to include commitments on responsible use of AI in the public sector; Red GEALC is supported by the OAS. Text not located; check whether it adopts the MIGDIA guidelines.

membership_note: The OAS Charter has been ratified by the independent states of the Americas; Nicaragua's withdrawal took effect in November 2023, and Cuba, although a member, does not participate in the Organization's activities.

members_source.comment: OAS Member States page, read 2026-10-21: 'All 35 independent states of the Americas have ratified the OAS Charter and are members of the Organization.' The page also notes AG/RES. 2438 (XXXIX-O/09) on Cuba. Nicaragua is excluded from the list because its denunciation of the OAS Charter took effect on 19 November 2023 (widely reported; the members page does not mention it).
